#1533. Spalletti apologises after Genoa defeat leaves Juventus level with Napoli on 14 points

Juventus lost 2-0 at Genoa on Serie A Matchday 9, a third league defeat in nine games that undid the good work of the win at Lecce. Napoli, the next visitors to Turin, now have the same points total.

The defeat came on 28 October 2026, with both Genoa goals arriving before half-time. Luciano Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. The result came three days after a 2-0 win at Lecce on Matchday 8. That win, built on first-half goals from Weston McKennie and Douglas Luiz, now looks like a false dawn.

Genoa needed little time to break through, and Ehizibue was the man to do it. His goal ended a 504-minute run without a Genoa goal against Juventus in Serie A, going back to an Albert Gudmundsson strike on 15 December 2023, Sportmediaset reported.

Baldanzi then exposed the Juventus defence again. Scoring and setting up a goal in one Serie A match was new for Baldanzi.

Juventus’s best chance of the first half came just before the interval. Kalulu shot off target after a pass from McKennie. Spalletti sent on Edon Zhegrova and Nick Woltemade for the second half. The changes did not help, and Genoa held firm. The win moved Daniele De Rossi’s side up to 10 points.

The coach did not hide from the performance. His team were beaten in every area of the pitch and must improve physically and in their fighting spirit, Spalletti told the club’s website. In his press conference he pointed to a lack of physical impact and to lost duels.

He also noted that the level shown at Lecce had not been repeated. There had been no training session between the two matches. That short turnaround is part of his explanation.

The evening got worse elsewhere. Napoli won 4-1 at Monza, with goals from Højlund, Politano, Rafa Marín and De Bruyne. Their coach, Massimiliano Allegri, watched from the stands. He was serving a two-match ban picked up against Roma.

Spalletti described Napoli as a very strong team. Both sides sit well behind the top of the table, so the meeting carries weight for each.

#1532. Cristiano Ronaldo QUITS international football after explosive fall-out with Portugal manager: Superstar, 41, announces retirement in emotional five-minute video

Published: 05:34 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 10:58 EDT, 5 November 2026

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his illustrious career in international football.

Ronaldo, 41, scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

His retirement comes just weeks after his explosive falling-out with new manager Jorge Jesus, which ended with Ronaldo abandoning Portugal's camp during the most recent international break in September and October.

It appeared as if he could return for the upcoming break this month for clashes with Denmark and Wales, but he has decided to step away after 23 years.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

The Al-Nassr star is hoping to pass the baton to his son, 16-year-old Cristiano Junior, who this week has been called up for Portugal's Under-17s.

Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 aged 18 and went on to play in six World Cups, a record he shares with Lionel Messi, as well as six European Championships, two Nations League finals, and a Confederations Cup.

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his illustrious international career with Portugal

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

He never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Ironically, his most memorable hour in a Portugal shirt was arguably when he wasn't playing. After getting injured during the 2016 Euros final, he cut such a passionate figure on the touchline, barking instructions to his team-mates, that he had practically taken over from manager Fernando Santos.

However, his dream of winning a World Cup always eluded him, and his best results were reaching the semi-finals in 2006 in Germany and the quarters in 2022 in Qatar.

His final act in football's greatest tournament was Portugal's 1-0 defeat by arch-rivals Spain at this summer's World Cup – a devastating day which saw him leave in tears.

And his final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner admitted he had at times 'failed' but was still proud

His time with Portugal in the last international break ended acrimoniously as he abandoned their camp after being left on the bench against Norway

Manager Jorge Jesus insisted that Ronaldo is welcome back, and did his team-mates

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 18-year international career.

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

The 41-year-old has scored scored 146 goals in 234 games - the most of anybody ever

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures.

It was a messy episode – not unlike how he left Manchester United for a second time in 2022 – and the question remains as to whether he would have still been playing had the row never occurred.

'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'A journey comes to an end that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever. When I look back and think about everything I experienced in the national team, I do not just see games, goals, records, or trophies. I see people. I see immigrants who, for 90 minutes, felt Portugal a little closer.

'I see millions of Portuguese people that I never met personally, but who were part of my life. Because at the end of everything, football is much greater than a game. Football is people. Throughout my career in the national team, I sought to surpass my limits. I wanted to win, I wanted to be the best, I wanted to make history.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'We believe again. Portugal will always need youngsters who dream of it, players who never give up, new generations who believe it is possible to reach where no one has reached. Because a country that continues to create new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.

'To my national team teammates, I want to leave a special word. Thank you for every run, for every hug, for every argument, for every silence before entering the pitch. For every victory we celebrated together and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. And you are part of my history. To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit men, staff, and so many people who worked with me over these years, my thank you.

'Many of you never appeared in these photographs. But without you, none of those photographs would have been possible. To my family, thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices, and the moments when the national team had to occupy a space that also belonged to you.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.

'That is a feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life. Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team ends. I leave with my head held high, proud of the path I walked and with the awareness that I gave everything I had for Portugal.

'But I will never stop being one of you. I will continue to suffer, to cheer, and to celebrate every victory of Portugal. I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realize that the greatest victory was having deserved to represent the best country in the world.

'Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a boy in Madeira, chasing a ball. The number seven jersey stays, the pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be in me. Farewell always, Cristiano Ronaldo.'

#1531. Sunday's Premier League predictions including Man Utd vs. Aston Villa, Crystal Palace vs. Liverpool

By Matthew Cooper | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Premier League predictions include Manchester United at home to Aston Villa, before struggling Crystal Palace take on Liverpool.

High-flying Brighton & Hove Albion will welcome Brentford to the Amex Stadium for Sunday's Premier League encounter.

The Seagulls head into the weekend in third spot in the Premier League table, while the Bees start matchday 10 in sixth position.

Brighton have scored at least three goals in each of their five competitive home wins this season, and while Brentford have drawn all four of their away league games this term, we think the Seagulls will make full use of their firepower to extend their unbeaten head-to-head home run with a relatively comfortable victory.

Ipswich Town play host to Bournemouth on Sunday afternoon looking for the win that could catapult them into the top half of the Premier League table.

While the Tractor Boys start the next batch of fixtures in 14th position, the Cherries are in eighth place after three successive victories in the top flight.

Ipswich will feel that their lighter schedule and week off from action gives them a clear advantage for this contest. However, we cannot back against a Bournemouth side who are free-scoring and searching for their eighth successive victory in all competitions.

Liverpool will hope to bounce back and deliver a fatal blow to Pierre Sage's hopes of remaining in charge of Crystal Palace when the two clash in the Premier League on Sunday at Selhurst Park.

The Reds are sixth in the top flight with 15 points after nine matchweeks, and the come into the weekend on the back of a 3-2 defeat against Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday, whereas Palace are 18th with just seven points and could end the weekend in last place.

Palace may boast the advantage of playing at home, but their lack of options in attack could cost them.

While Liverpool have been far from perfect in the final third, they have often taken three points from Selhurst Park, and it would not be surprising if they claimed another victory on the road this weekend.

Needing nothing short of a minor miracle to replicate their 2025-26 feats against Chelsea, Sunderland host the Blues in Sunday's Premier League fixture at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats trail their visitors by 16 places and 11 points in the Premier League table at the time of writing and face Xabi Alonso's well-rested men after a sobering defeat in Europe too.

Fatigue should not play a significant role for Sunderland on Sunday given the alterations Le Bris made in midweek, but backing the Black Cats to get anything out of any Premier League game at present is a tough ask.

Therefore, even a Pedro-less Chelsea side - working on a full week's worth of rest - should stroll to victory, with an increasingly familiar clean sheet in tow.

Desperate to steer clear of the Premier League's relegation zone, Manchester United will host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

The Red Devils are hoping to build on their midweek Champions League victory, while the Lions are keen to get back on track after a three-game winless run.

Man United may have won in midweek, but they were the beneficiaries of major errors from the Roma defence, and are unlikely to repeat the feat on Sunday.

Villa are on a three-game winless run that has spanned three different competitions, yet they will be optimistic about getting the better of their struggling hosts.

#1530. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton and Hove Albion Verbruggen; Wieffer, Vuskovic, Boscagli, Dunk; Gross, Ayari; Gomez, Hinshelwood, De Cuyper; Rutter

Subs Steele, Strujik, Costinha, Svoboda, Osman, Yalcouye, David, Kostoulas, Yohanna

Aston Villa Bizot; Cash, Torres, Lindelof, Maatsen; Barkley, Kamara; McGinn, Gomes, Hemmings; Buendia

Subs Suzuki, Mings, Ruggeri, Bogarde, Alysson, Rowe, Burrowes, Garnacho, Lynch

Manchester City Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Lewis; Semenyo, Foden, O’Reilly; Haaland

Subs Rulli, Ait-Nouri, Nunes, Reis, Kovacic, Cherki, Gonzalez, Grealish, Marmoush

Bournemouth Petrovic; Smith, Silva, Hill, Truffert; Cook, Scott; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Subs Dennis, Diakite, Gannon-Doak, Toth, Sanchez, Brooks, Adams, Rodriguez, Jebbison

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Representing Aston Villa 👊 pic.twitter.com/JjqgYhBzwb

TEAM NEWS! 🚨 Here's how we start 🆚 Villa! 👊 pic.twitter.com/nnFj5swsdg

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

🔵 TEAM NEWS🍒The first #afcb team of the new Premier League season 👊 pic.twitter.com/uJhTI01Jld

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#1528. Carnevali calls Juventus situation ‘not acceptable’ as squad enters retreat before Napoli

Juventus will stay together in a training retreat at the JTC Continassa from Friday 30 October until Sunday's game against Napoli, after a blunt meeting between Giovanni Carnevali, the players and Luciano Spalletti. That home fixture is now widely seen as decisive for the coach's future and the direction of the season.

A direct meeting with chief executive Giovanni Carnevali has put the Juventus players and their coach under heavy pressure before Napoli’s visit.

The trigger was the loss in Genoa. Kingsley Ehizibue struck in the 12th minute, and Tommaso Baldanzi added a second in the 28th. Spalletti apologised to the supporters afterwards. He said his side had been beaten in every area. He added that they had to raise their physical level and fighting spirit.

The squad travelled back by train overnight. The players went to the Continassa the next morning. Management spoke to them there before training. Carnevali reminded them of their responsibilities to the owners, the club and the fans. He said the coaching staff still had the club’s trust, Adnkronos reported. He also asked for a strong and concrete reaction on the pitch. With the club’s agreement, Spalletti then chose to keep the players together at the training centre until kick-off.

Clubs rarely call this kind of retreat. It shows how serious the mood is at the Continassa. The message from the top is twofold. Public backing for the coaching staff comes paired with pressure for results. That places heavy weight on a single fixture.

Both sides have four wins, two draws and three defeats from nine games, Corriere dello Sport reported. Napoli sit seventh and Juventus eighth.

The gap lies in front of goal. Napoli have scored 17 times. Juventus have managed 11. Juventus have conceded only 10, however. Those figures are consistent with a side whose problems lie more in attack than in defence. A reaction against Napoli would need goals as well as fighting spirit.

Napoli will be without their coach. Massimiliano Allegri’s two-match ban covers their league games against Monza and Juventus. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea also fined him 10,000 euros. The sanction followed his abuse of match officials and later behaviour in the changing rooms during Napoli’s 3-3 draw with Roma. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri later said he had decided to drop it. That leaves Juventus facing a Napoli side without Allegri in charge at a moment when their own coach is under pressure.

The last meeting between the sides in Turin, on 25 January 2026, ended in a 3-0 Juventus win at the Allianz Stadium.

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November 2026, with kick-off at 20:45.

#1527. Sunday's Serie A predictions including Napoli vs. Lazio, Inter Milan vs. Como

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 08 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 08 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Serie A predictions cover an intriguing round of fixtures, with AC Milan travelling to Genoa, Juventus visiting Fiorentina and Atalanta BC taking on Monza, while Napoli host Lazio and defending champions Inter Milan welcome Como to the San Siro.

Trending in very different directions, Serie A leaders Lazio will visit a faltering Napoli side on Sunday, as Stadio Maradona hosts the lunchtime kickoff.

While the home side are struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, their southern rivals have posted nine wins from 10 and are yet to taste defeat in the league.

Struggling in Serie A, facing another early exit from Europe and burdened by a huge absence list, Napoli are set to lose three games on the spin.

While Lazio's stellar run will surely end soon, they can exploit their hosts' shaky defence and post a seventh straight win.

Atalanta BC will be looking to end a six-match winless run across all competitions when they travel to Monza on Sunday for matchday 11 of the Serie A campaign.

Maurizio Sarri's side sit 13th in the Italian top-flight table after collecting just 11 points from their opening 10 matches, leaving them four points above the relegation zone, where the hosts occupy 18th place.

Monza's defensive problems make it difficult to see them containing Atalanta, who have dominated this fixture in recent years, and that could provide the visitors with a good opportunity to end their current winless run.

After a week of highs and lows, AC Milan will head towards the international break with a tough trip to Genoa on Sunday afternoon.

Before they clash at Stadio Ferraris, the hosts have actually claimed more points from their last five Serie A games than the inconsistent Rossoneri.

Allied to two cup wins at Stadio Ferraris, Genoa have won half of their first six home games in Serie A, so Milan will be put through a stern test.

While Amorim's men are leaking too many goals, De Rossi's side have found their shooting boots, and that could produce an end-to-end draw.

Having suffered derby defeat and slipped off top spot in Serie A, reigning champions Inter Milan must try to get back on track when they welcome record-breaking Como to San Siro on Sunday.

Following four intense meetings last term, the regional rivals are currently separated by two points, with both trailing surprise leaders Lazio.

Inter's defence is creaking at the seams, and without the leadership of their inspirational skipper they are always more vulnerable.

Although free-flowing Como must be starting to tire, recent events suggest it is time to finally slay the Nerazzurri.

Sending Serie A into the international break, old foes Fiorentina and Juventus will clash at Stadio Franchi on Sunday night.

While the Viola are still seeking their first home win of the season, fallen giants Juve have been left trailing Italy's top six.

Both teams have been too inconsistent to match their pre-season aims, making the outcome on Sunday night quite tough to predict.

Juve are assured of a hostile reception in Florence, but the hosts tend to wilt in front of their own fans - so, all three points will go back to Turin.

#1526. Modric hints he could continue beyond 2026-27 season: “As long as I feel this way”

Luka Modric has hinted that he could continue playing beyond this season, having made Milan his home since arriving in 2025.

In the summer, after some speculation prior to the World Cup, Modric put pen to paper and extended his contract with Milan for another season. It was a huge boost for Ruben Amorim, who pushed for the Croatian to stay and help shape the new Milan.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A few months ago, Modric also announced that he would continue with the Croatian national team, deciding not to retire after the World Cup. It’s a pretty clear signal that he still feels in great shape and perhaps could continue beyond this season.

Speaking to this week’s edition of SportWeek, as transcribed by MilanPress, Modric shared his thoughts on the derby and the project at Milan. He also said that as long as he feels good, he will continue to play football, hinting that the 2027-28 season might not be his last.

“It was a fantastic victory and I think it was our best performance of the season. We deserved these three points, which we really needed, both for our morale and for our confidence.

“We are growing as a team, and if we can limit the dips in form that can occur over a season, we will have a chance to fight for the title, which remains our goal.

“We are putting the coach’s ideas into practice better and better, we are moving in the right direction, and our stadium is driving us: the Milan fans are incredible.”

“I feel good and I still have the passion, ambition, and strength. As long as I feel this way, I want to keep playing. I’m also loved at Milan. I had no doubts this summer, after speaking with Amorim and the club: they wanted me to stay and I just needed to feel wanted.

“Milan is my team, and I want to help the younger players develop,” he stated.

#1525. Jeff Ekhator back in Juventus group training after injury nightmare

Jeff Ekhator has finally rejoined his Juventus teammates on the training pitch. The young striker, signed from Genoa in the summer, took part in a full group session at the Continassa on Friday for the first time since a run of muscle problems that has so far kept him out of every competitive game in black and white.

His return gives Luciano Spalletti one more name to consider in a week when the squad has been kept together at the training centre ahead of Sunday’s visit of Napoli.

Juventus announced the permanent deal on 1 July, and Football Italia put the fee at €16m plus add ons. The 19 year old has barely been available since.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, who credits Sky Sport Italia with the news, his troubles began in the very first friendly of pre-season against Basel. He recovered in time to be named in the squad for the second Serie A round against Parma, where he stayed on the bench, but broke down again a few days later and has spent roughly two further months on the sidelines.

Di Marzio describes the forward as fully recovered, and Friday’s session with the rest of the group was his first since that setback.

Jeff Ekhator signs for Juventus from Genoa on a permanent deal! ⚪️⚫️ Welcome to the club, Jeff! 🙌

Nobody should expect Ekhator to be rushed into the starting eleven after so long without match practice. Football Italia sees him more as an extra option from the bench, giving Spalletti a third centre forward alongside Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani.

That alone matters for a side that has struggled for goals. Juventus have scored 11 times in nine league games, and the 2-0 defeat at Genoa on Wednesday, covered in our report on Spalletti’s apology, left them level on 14 points with Napoli.

The timing of his comeback is notable. After the Genoa loss, chief executive Giovanni Carnevali met the players and the coach, and Spalletti then decided to keep the squad together at the training ground until kick off, as explained in our piece on the Juventus retreat.

Napoli come to the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 1 November for Matchday 10, with kick off at 20:45 local time. According to the club’s own match notes, it is the first time since April 2021 that the two sides meet on the same number of points in Serie A.

Whether Ekhator makes the matchday squad will become clear when Spalletti names his group. Either way, having a fit young striker back in training is a rare piece of good news for Juventus this week.

Sources: Gianluca Di Marzio, Football Italia, Juventus

Sergio Lattanzi has followed Juventus since the days of the Trap, when Serie A felt like the centre of the football world and the Bianconeri were its undisputed rulers. Born and raised in Turin, he developed an early obsession with the tactical patterns that made Juventus so difficult to beat, and that curiosity never left him. He watches matches with a notepad nearby and a tendency to rewind passages of play more times than anyone around him considers reasonable.

#1523. Now will the FA put their money where their mouth is? England chiefs and UEFA must decide whether to back rival Japanese bid to FIFA president Gianni Infantino after slamming World Cup controversial sell-off plan

Published: 08:23 EDT, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 11:00 EDT, 5 November 2026

The FA and UEFA face a dilemma over whether to support a bid to challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency after honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announced his decision to stand.

Alongside the FA, UEFA have spearheaded opposition to Infantino following the collapse of his botched deal to sell stakes in the World Cup.

However, despite declaring Infantino 'has lost the confidence of UEFA' and threatening to boycott the World Cup, the European governing body have so far failed to come up with a candidate to challenge him at the March election in Rabat.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin decided against a run for the FIFA presidency, opting instead to focus on securing another term at the top of European football.

At a meeting of the FA Council last month FA chair Debbie Hewitt demanded answers over the World Cup sell-off plan - and decision to suspend the ban of US striker Folarin Balogun after pressure from Donald Trump. She said: 'The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting.'

But there is a growing feeling that a European candidate would struggle to secure sufficient support from the rest of the world, while Infantino believes he already has enough votes to secure re-election, making it difficult to find a credible challenger.

Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima has announced a decision to stand for FIFA presidency

Tashima will run against the controversial current president Gianni Infantino (left)

That said, FIFA Council member and Japanese FA bigwig Tashima could split the Asian vote and is well respected in Europe.

With Tashima - the first candidate to secure the backing of a national association - declaring his intention to run, pressure is now mounting on the FA and UEFA to either support his bid or put forward a candidate of their own, having called for Infantino to step down.

It follows former Tottenham and Switzerland footballer Ramon Vega making a public leadership bid on Wednesday, though it is unclear whether he could obtain the backing of enough national associations.

Candidates require the support of five football associations to run for the presidency and must pass eligibility checks by November 18.

Tashima is the first candidate with a realistic chance to announce an intention to run before the November 18 deadline, where the support of five national associations is required.

Speaking to Japanese newspaper Sports Nippon, Tashima said: ‘I am grateful that I can make this announcement with the full support of the Japan Football Association.

‘It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built. What FIFA needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.’

#1521. Juventus and Napoli meet level on 14 points as Allegri ban and Lobotka injury bite

Juventus host Napoli at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday with both sides on 14 points and both short of key figures. Spalletti is missing seven players, while Napoli lose their suspended coach and their midfield organiser Lobotka.

Juventus and Napoli go into Sunday’s Serie A Matchday 10 meeting at the Allianz Stadium level on points. Both benches will look different. Napoli will be without their head coach, with assistant Landucci on the bench. Spalletti is still missing seven players.

Allegri was sent off in Napoli’s 3-3 home draw with Roma. Serie A’s sporting judge then punished him for disrespectful remarks to the match officials. The ban covered the trip to Monza on 28 October and now the visit to Juventus. Napoli first announced an appeal. Allegri dropped it, saying he feared the ban could rise to four matches. The suspension is now final.

Napoli also lost Lobotka at Monza. He was stretchered off just after the 15th minute following a challenge with Mangas. The club’s medical update found damage to the tibiofibular syndesmosis in his left ankle, without instability. He also has a low-grade injury to the anterior talofibular ligament. He has started rehabilitation, with Napoli aiming for a return against Fiorentina in the Coppa Italia on 16 December. Badiashile and Neres are also injured.

The Juventus list is longer. Yildiz is expected back in early December after a foot operation, Sky Sport Italia reported. Thuram, who had knee surgery, is due back in early 2027. Locatelli is out until 2027 after a lateral meniscus operation. Grabara, with a right-knee ACL injury, is effectively out for the season.

Nico González (right soleus), Çelik (left hamstring) and Conceição (shoulder dislocation) are all expected back after the international break. There is one return. Young forward Ekhator is available again.

Juventus arrive after an uneven run. Lazio won 3-0 away at Juventus on 18 October. Spalletti’s side then won at Lecce on 25 October, with goals from McKennie and Douglas Luiz. Genoa won the next game through first-half goals from Ehizibue and Baldanzi. Koopmeiners hit the crossbar in stoppage time.

After the Genoa defeat, chief executive Carnevali held a long meeting with the squad. He told them to change course straight away, especially in their mentality. Spalletti then announced the squad would stay together from Friday evening until the Napoli game. The club wants the response to come from the players on the pitch rather than from a change of coach. Enough has been said about the poor performance against Ferencvaros already, so let’s just leave it at the fact that it was incredibly disappointing. As such, a strong response is needed immediately in the league, taking on Genoa tomorrow.

The Rossoblu have been in very good form lately, winning four of their last five games, after what was a relegation-worthy start to the season. In other words, they have hit their stride just before the Rossoneri clash, which isn’t ideal.

In the latest podcast episode, which was recorded the day after the derby win, Oliver, Anthony and Ahmed briefly shared their thoughts on the Marassi encounter.

Since the boys previewed both the Ferencvaros game and the Genoa game in the episode, spending most of the time talking about the derby, their predictions weren’t exactly lengthy. We even got a “whoever plays better will win” from Oliver!

Oliver: “It’s a tough game, they’ve got a good team with some decent players. Whoever plays better will win (laughs). Jokes aside, this might be a draw with a little bit of European hangover for us.”

Anthony: “Whoever plays better will win, what a prediction… I’m going 2-1 to Milan [prediction added in post].”
